simple.meaning: בְּנֵי יַעֲקָן (Bᵉnêy Yaʻăqân) is a Hebrew word meaning “Bene-Jaakan , a place in the Desert.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בְּנֵי יַעֲקָן (H1142) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Numbers 33:31, with occurrences in Numbers.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בְּנֵי יַעֲקָן (H1142) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in בְּנֵי יַעֲקָן (H1142) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: בְּנֵי יַעֲקָן (Bᵉnêy Yaʻăqân) / H1142 is traced through Numbers 33:31, Numbers 33:32 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: Bene-Jaakan , a place in the Desert
definitions.full: H1142. Bene Yaaqan יַעֲָק֑ן בְּנֵי proper name, of a location a station of Israel in wilderness Num 33:31-32 , (= יעקן בני בְּאֵרוֺת Deut 10:6 q. v.; compare also יַעֲקָ֑ן 1Chr 1:42 = וַעֲקָ֑ן Gen 36:27 , & Di Num 33:31 ).
definitions.rootNote: from the plural of 1121 and 3292 ; sons of Yaakan;

occurrences.englishText: They traveled from Moseroth, and encamped in Bene Jaakan.
They traveled from Bene Jaakan, and encamped in Hor Haggidgad.
